title: LRU Catalog Cache

visible.label: Basic put, get, and LRU eviction
visible.script:
cache = LRUCache(2)
cache.put(101, 50)
cache.put(102, 75)
assert cache.get(101) == 50
cache.put(103, 90)
assert cache.get(102) == -1
assert cache.get(103) == 90
assert cache.get(101) == 50

visible.label: Updating existing key refreshes recency without evicting
visible.script:
cache = LRUCache(2)
cache.put(1, 10)
cache.put(2, 20)
cache.put(1, 15)
cache.put(3, 30)
assert cache.get(1) == 15
assert cache.get(2) == -1
assert cache.get(3) == 30

hidden.label: Capacity 1 replaces single entry
hidden.script:
cache = LRUCache(1)
cache.put(1, 1)
assert cache.get(1) == 1
cache.put(2, 2)
assert cache.get(1) == -1
assert cache.get(2) == 2

hidden.label: Missing get does not evict or reorder
hidden.script:
cache = LRUCache(2)
cache.put(1, 1)
cache.put(2, 2)
assert cache.get(99) == -1
cache.put(3, 3)
assert cache.get(1) == -1
assert cache.get(2) == 2
assert cache.get(3) == 3

hidden.label: Repeated updates keep size bounded
hidden.inputDisplay: LRUCache(2): overwrite key 1 three times then insert key 2 and 3
hidden.script:
cache = LRUCache(2)
cache.put(1, 10)
cache.put(1, 20)
cache.put(2, 30)
cache.put(1, 25)
cache.put(3, 40)
assert cache.get(2) == -1
assert cache.get(1) == 25
assert cache.get(3) == 40

hidden.label: Multi-step recency trace
hidden.script:
cache = LRUCache(3)
cache.put(1, 10)
cache.put(2, 20)
cache.put(3, 30)
assert cache.get(1) == 10
cache.put(4, 40)
assert cache.get(2) == -1
assert cache.get(3) == 30
cache.put(5, 50)
assert cache.get(1) == -1
assert cache.get(4) == 40
assert cache.get(3) == 30
assert cache.get(5) == 50

hidden.label: Large O(1) cache performance test
hidden.script:
cache = LRUCache(5000)
for i in range(25000):
    cache.put(i, i * 10)
    if i >= 10:
        assert cache.get(i - 10) == (i - 10) * 10
assert cache.get(0) == -1
assert cache.get(24999) == 249990

hints: You need O(1) average lookup by key AND O(1) tracking of which key was least recently used.
In Python, collections.OrderedDict provides move_to_end(key) and popitem(last=False) in O(1), or you can pair a plain dict with a doubly linked list of nodes.

Pseudocode (OrderedDict):
  init(capacity): store capacity and OrderedDict()
  get(key): if key missing return -1; move_to_end(key); return value
  put(key, val): if capacity <= 0 return; set/update key and move_to_end(key); if len > capacity popitem(last=False)
